title: An Introduction to Torsors in Mathematics with a View Toward $Σ$-Protocols in Cryptography
summary: This paper provides a preparatory introduction to torsors, written with a view toward later applications in the author's work. Rather than aiming at a comprehensive survey, the exposition focuses on those aspects of torsors that are most useful for understanding torsor-based reasoning: group actions, orbits, free transitive actions, the absence of a canonically chosen origin, and the interpretation of group elements as transports between points.
